commands.command: cargo test -p repopact-provider-github transport::download_rejects_a_truncated_body (new test, no production code change needed)
commands.summary: Empirically verified, rather than assumed, that a server declaring a Content-Length larger than what it actually sends before closing the connection is already caught by the underlying HTTP stack (hyper's length-framed body reader surfaces an io error on early close) and correctly propagates through ReqwestTransport::download as a typed download failure with the partial destination file removed by the existing error path. No new truncation-detection code was needed; this closes the exact Checkpoint C gap by proving the existing architecture already handles it correctly, which was previously merely assumed.

commands.command: New: real 5xx tests (500, 503) and a real redirect-loop-exhaustion test (a persistent, non-one-shot local server answering every connection with a 302 back to itself) against ReqwestTransport::download
commands.summary: Closes the remaining two Checkpoint C gaps. The redirect-loop test proves MAX_REDIRECTS is enforced against a server that never stops redirecting -- the test server accepts at most MAX_REDIRECTS+1 connections total and then completes normally (a correctly-bounded client makes no more than that), rather than merely asserting a documented constant.

A genuine TLS certificate-validation failure through the production rustls-backed reqwest client on both the download and REST GET code paths -- no insecure-TLS bypass exists anywhere in this codebase to disable for the test. badssl.com is a long-standing public test service purpose-built for exactly this class of test, the same live-network-proof convention this module already uses for octocat/Hello-World. Both tests pass: the self-signed certificate is rejected, no partial file is left behind.

commands.command: Fixed a real gap in transport.rs's download error-body handling: a non-2xx response body was previously embedded into the TransportError message via String::from_utf8_lossy with only a raw 2048-byte cap and no redaction
commands.summary: Now passes through repopact_remote_provider::redact::redact() and is additionally bounded to 200 characters after redaction, mirroring rest.rs's own error-body handling for the REST GET path. New download_error_body_is_bounded_and_redacted_even_when_hostile test proves a hostile response body containing a synthetic canary token, an Authorization-shaped value, and a 10,000-character padding string never survives into the resulting error message and that the message stays well under 500 characters regardless.

commands.command: New: download_reports_retry_after_on_a_secondary_rate_limit_403 (real local socket) + provider.rs map_download_error extended to recognize a 403 accompanied by Retry-After as ProviderRateLimited (secondary rate limit), and 5xx statuses generically as ProviderProtocolError, mirroring rest.rs's own REST-path rate-limit/error taxonomy
commands.summary: GitHub rate-limit semantics (Phase 4) are now represented identically on both the REST and download paths: primary rate limit (429 or X-RateLimit-Remaining=0), and secondary rate limit (403 + Retry-After) both map to the same typed ProviderRateLimited code with the server-reported retry timing carried in the (bounded, redacted) detail text. No automatic retry loop exists anywhere in this codebase.

commands.command: New dedicated token-canary redaction sweep: repopact-remote-provider/src/error.rs gains 4 tests injecting synthetic ghu_REPOPACT_CANARY_.../ghr_REPOPACT_CANARY_... tokens and a credential-bearing URL into RemoteProviderError::new's detail argument, asserting absence from .detail, Display, Debug, and serialized JSON
commands.summary: Dedicated GH-013 evidence, not merely incidental: proves RemoteProviderError::new's existing redact() call actually closes this leakage vector for every consumer of the type (not just the specific call sites Checkpoint A/B/C happened to test), across every representation (struct field, Display, Debug, serde). Combined with the new transport-level hostile-body test above, this covers the token-leakage requirement across both the construction boundary and the network-response boundary.

commands.command: New structural governance-boundary test: rust/crates/repopact-mutation/tests/remote_provider_governance_boundary.rs (3 tests) asserting repopact-mutation/repopact-graph/repopact-core's Cargo.toml manifests never depend on repopact-mobile-acquisition, repopact-remote-provider, or repopact-provider-github
commands.summary: Dedicated GH-013/Phase 8 evidence that GitHub/remote-provider metadata cannot be elevated into governance/mutation approval authority: confirmed none of the three crates depend on any remote-provider-related crate today, so WorkspaceRecord::remote_snapshot_provenance (or any other remote/provider value) is not merely unused by governance/mutation logic -- it is not even reachable at compile time.
